chunks: And from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Hakim ibn Aiman al-Hannat, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"A man does not swear an oath except based on his knowledge."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq, establishes the condition of certainty (yaqin) for the validity of oaths, preventing the sin of perjury or false swearing. In Shia jurisprudence, this principle underscores that an oath is only binding and truthful if the swearer possesses genuine knowledge of the matter, distinguishing it from mere opinion or guesswork. It serves as a foundational ethical guideline for maintaining integrity in verbal commitments and legal declarations.
